title: What If 'Just a Second' Froze Time for 10 Minutes?
sources: Original concept: 'just a second' as a literal time-freeze trigger (creative speculation)
Time perception psychology: subjective time dilation in boredom vs flow states (Wittmann & Paulus, 2008)

lines.text: What if every time someone said just a second, time actually froze for ten minutes?
lines.caps: WHAT IF *EVERY TIME | YOU SAID *JUST A SECOND | TIME *FROZE | FOR TEN *MINUTES?

lines.text: You're brushing your teeth, you mutter it, and suddenly you're late for work.
Your boss says it in a meeting — the whole room freezes. Ten minutes gone.
lines.caps: BOSS *SAYS IT | WHOLE ROOM *FREEZES | TEN MINUTES *GONE

lines.text: You say it on a first date. The awkward silence becomes ten minutes of frozen stares.
The microwave beeps. You say it. Your burrito's cold but the timer hasn't moved.
But if you say it right before a deadline, you get infinite time. Everyone else? Frozen.
So maybe just say one moment instead.
